rows.reason: The round-5 fault is fixed: the first sentence is now two plain sentences with the contrast kept ('In lines 13 and 14 he returns a cardigan whose owner has left.' / 'Yet on line 33 his own jumper goes in "the Friday box".'). Every citation checks: the leaver's cardigan is across lines 13 and 14, 'the Friday box' is on line 33, 'It won't fit me next year.' is on line 47, 'longer than the answer needed' is on line 48. Quotations are word for word, the 5 sentences run 12, 10, 9, 16 and 16 words, there is no first person, and the key comes only at the end. The key is still the one defensible answer. But the last sentence fails in two ways. (1) Dropping line 38's "September football trials" removed the only thing that ties the trials sheet to next year. 'He is giving up next year, so the trials sheet has a space he won't fill.' now asserts that link: nothing in the script says when the trials are, and the stem does not say either. A child cannot see why giving up next year bears on this sheet. This is the same fault rounds 2 and 3 were refused for, moved one step along. The script also never sends the child to the sheet itself (lines 37 to 39). (2) 'He is giving up next year' reads most naturally as a future event, 'next year he will give up', not as 'giving up ON next year'. Round 4 said 'letting go of next year'; the dropped 'on' changes the meaning. Fix: keep sentences 3 and 4 as they are. Restore the September link and the 'on' in the last step, e.g. 'He is giving up on next year, and the trials on line 38 are in "September".' then 'So the room at the bottom is a space he won't fill.' To stay within 5 sentences, fold sentences 1 and 2 into one that keeps the contrast word, e.g. 'He returns a leaver's cardigan in lines 13 and 14, yet gives his own away.' The fault is in the script, not the question.
